subject: Chemistry
title: Elimination vs Substitution: Alcohol or Alkene?
summary: An alkyl halide with a β-hydrogen can be attacked at carbon (substitution) or lose HX (elimination). The conditions decide which wins. In this lesson: OH- as a nucleophile or as a base, aqueous vs alcoholic KOH, 1° vs 3° halides, the size of the base (tert-butoxide), temperature, and two solved questions: bromoethane + aqueous KOH and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane + alcoholic KOH.

notes.title: Elimination vs Substitution
notes.blurb: two jobs for oh⁻, what decides, solved questions

keyPoints: **Medium**: Water **cages** OH⁻. Alcohol gives **ethoxide**, a stronger base.
**Halide · base**: tert-Butoxide **cannot reach C**. It takes an outer **β-H** instead.

list: **As a nucleophile** it attacks the carbon bearing X: **substitution** → alcohol (CH₃CH₂Br → CH₃CH₂OH).
**As a base** it removes a β-hydrogen: **elimination** → alkene (CH₃CH₂Br → CH₂=CH₂).

head: Factor
Substitution
Elimination
rows: aqueous KOH (OH⁻ caged by water: acts as a nucleophile)
alcoholic KOH (ethoxide, a stronger base), heat

blocks.p: NCERT: the product depends on the nature of the alkyl halide, the strength and size of the base or nucleophile, and the reaction conditions.

list: ✗ Aqueous KOH gives the alkene (it gives the alcohol).
✗ A bulky base gives more substitution (it cannot reach the carbon, so it eliminates).

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: 1-Bromopropane is reacted with the reagents in List-I to give the products in List-II. List-I: A. KOH (alc), B. KCN (alc), C. AgNO₂, D. H₃CCOOAg. List-II: I. Nitrile, II. Ester, III. Alkene, IV. Nitroalkane.
pyq.explain: Alc. KOH: elimination → propene (III). KCN: CN⁻ attacks through C → nitrile (I). AgNO₂: through N → nitroalkane (IV). CH₃COOAg → ester (II).

pyq.q: Statement (I): Alcohols are formed when alkyl chlorides are treated with aqueous potassium hydroxide by elimination reaction. Statement (II): In alcoholic potassium hydroxide, alkyl chlorides form alkenes by abstracting the hydrogen from the β-carbon.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
pyq.explain: Aqueous KOH gives alcohols by substitution, not elimination: I is incorrect. II is correct (β-elimination).
